prompt.context: Our client is a large media company in Los Angeles. It currently has two offices — one in Santa Monica and one in Century City. They have decided to consolidate their operations into one location and will choose one of their existing buildings.
prompt.question: Which office location should our client choose for consolidation, and why?

clarifying_info.q: Does the client own or lease the buildings?
clarifying_info.a: Both buildings are under lease for 10 years.

clarifying_info.q: How much space does the client need?
clarifying_info.a: The client requires 100,000 sq ft of space.

clarifying_info.q: What are the buildings currently used for?
clarifying_info.a: Santa Monica houses Video Games operations (200,000 sq ft at $40/sq ft/year, build-out cost $1,500K over 10 years). Century City houses DVD operations (400,000 sq ft at $40/sq ft/year, build-out cost $500K over 10 years).
The client can sub-lease any and all unused space. Assume they can sub-lease 100% of unused space.

clarifying_info.q: What are the local vacancy rates?
clarifying_info.a: Santa Monica has a 10% average vacancy rate; Century City has an 18% average vacancy rate.

clarifying_info.q: What sub-lease rates can the client charge?
clarifying_info.a: $40/sq ft/year for Santa Monica space; $30/sq ft/year for Century City space (higher vacancy in Century City means lower achievable sub-lease price).

framework: Evaluate economics of each option: total annual costs (rent + build-out) minus sub-lease income for both scenarios
Identify key cost drivers: lease obligations (locked in for 10 years on both buildings), build-out costs to prepare chosen office, sub-lease revenue from unused/vacated space
Assess non-financial factors: workforce integration, proximity to clients/customers, proximity to employee homes, cultural and political integration challenges
Synthesize findings into a clear recommendation with risks and next steps

questions.prompt: Calculate the annual financial impact of occupying Santa Monica only vs. Century City only.
questions.guidance: Candidate should recognize both leases are already locked in — both rent obligations are sunk/fixed costs regardless of choice. Key variables are: (1) build-out cost amortized over 10 years, (2) sub-lease income from the occupied building's unused space (total minus 100k sq ft needed), and (3) sub-lease income from the fully vacated building. Century City is financially superior by approximately $1.1M/year.

math.setup: Client needs 100k sq ft. Both leases are 10 years. Sub-lease rates: SM=$40, CC=$30. Build-out costs amortized: SM=$150k/yr, CC=$50k/yr.
steps: OPTION A sub-lease income: SM unused = (200k-100k)×$40=$4,000,000; CC fully vacated = 400k×$30=$12,000,000; Total sub-lease = $16,000,000/yr
OPTION B sub-lease income: CC unused = (400k-100k)×$30=$9,000,000; SM fully vacated = 200k×$40=$8,000,000; Total sub-lease = $17,000,000/yr
Marginal difference: Century City is better by $8,150,000 - $7,050,000 = $1,100,000/yr
math.answer: Occupy Century City: net annual cost of -$7,050,000 vs. -$8,150,000 for Santa Monica. Century City is better by $1.1M per year ($11M over 10 years).

questions.prompt: Besides economics, what else should the client consider when choosing which office to consolidate into?
questions.guidance: Strong answers cover: workforce integration issues (morale, culture clash between Video Games and DVD teams), proximity to clients and customers (which location better serves external stakeholders), proximity to where employees live (commute burden; use HR zip code data to analyze), office politics and talent retention risk during transition.

questions.prompt: How would you recommend the client inform its employees about this move?
questions.guidance: No single perfect answer — candidate should identify multiple communication options and weigh pros/cons. Options include: (1) company-wide meeting — broad but impersonal, harder to manage reactions; (2) start with top employees to secure retention before wider announcement — protects key talent but risks leaks; (3) email/memo — efficient but cold, no dialogue; (4) one-on-one discussions between managers and employees — most personalized but time-intensive at scale. Candidate should defend their preferred approach while acknowledging its downsides and suggest how to mitigate them.

brainstorming.prompt: Besides the economics, what non-financial issues should our client consider when consolidating offices?

categories.name: Workforce Integration
ideas: Culture clash between Video Games and DVD teams
Morale impact on employees of the office that is being vacated
Risk of talent loss during transition
Management structure changes and reporting lines

categories.name: Employee Commute & Location
ideas: Proximity of each office to where employees currently live
Analysis of employee zip codes via HR to quantify commute burden
Availability of public transit to each location
Parking and transportation costs for employees

categories.name: Client & Customer Proximity
ideas: Which location is closer to key clients or partners
Industry cluster effects (e.g., entertainment industry hub proximity)
Impact on client-facing teams and meeting logistics

categories.name: Operational Continuity
ideas: Disruption to ongoing projects during the move
Timing of move relative to lease expiry or project milestones

recommendation: Consolidate operations into Century City — it is financially superior by $1.1M per year ($11M over the 10-year lease period) due to lower build-out costs and higher total sub-lease income
Develop a phased communication and change management plan to retain key talent and manage workforce integration
risks: Higher vacancy rate in Century City (18%) could make it harder to sub-lease the Santa Monica building at the assumed $40/sq ft rate — actual sub-lease income may be lower
Workforce attrition if key Video Games employees are unwilling to commute to Century City
Cultural integration challenges between the two previously separate teams
Sub-lease assumptions may not hold if the real estate market deteriorates
next_steps: Use HR data to map employee home zip codes and assess commute impact for both options
Draft a phased employee communication plan, starting with senior staff retention conversations
Engage a real estate broker to validate achievable sub-lease rates and time-to-lease assumptions for both buildings
Model downside scenario where Santa Monica space is only partially sub-leased to stress-test the Century City decision
